# `silk/i8`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Eight-bit signed integers for compact values, byte-level formats, and narrow arithmetic.

## When to use
Use `i8` when an external format or data structure requires exactly eight signed bits. Prefer a
wider integer for general arithmetic: the small range makes accidental overflow easy.

## Details
Ordinary arithmetic, narrowing conversions, division by zero, and invalid shift counts trap.
Choose `checked*` when failure is data, `wrapping*` for arithmetic modulo 2^8, or `saturating*`
when results should clamp to [`MIN`](#MIN) or [`MAX`](#MAX). Signed right shifts preserve the sign bit.

Decimal [`parse`](#parse) consumes the complete input and distinguishes malformed text from a value
outside the i8 range. Use [`Format`](./format.md#Format) with `Format.display` for defaults or `Format.displayWith`
for explicit options. Both operations stream through a mutable `Writer` without `Allocator`.

## Gotchas
[`MIN`](#MIN) has no positive i8 counterpart, so ordinary [`negate`](#negate) traps for that one value.

## Examples
### Select the boundary policy for negation
```silk
import silk.i8

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  if i8.wrappingNegate(i8.MIN) != i8.MIN {
    return 1
  }
  if i8.saturatingNegate(i8.MIN) != i8.MAX {
    return 2
  }
  return 42
}
```

Import as `i8` with `import silk.i8`.

<a id="negate"></a>

## `negate`

```silk
pub fn negate(value: i8) -> i8
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value` and traps when `value` is [`MIN`](#MIN). Use
this function when that boundary is a program error.

<a id="wrappingNegate"></a>

## `wrappingNegate`

```silk
pub fn wrappingNegate(value: i8) -> i8
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value`, wrapped to the `i8` range. [`MIN`](#MIN)
stays [`MIN`](#MIN). Use this function for deliberate modulo arithmetic.

<a id="saturatingNegate"></a>

## `saturatingNegate`

```silk
pub fn saturatingNegate(value: i8) -> i8
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value`, clamped to the `i8` range. [`MIN`](#MIN)
becomes [`MAX`](#MAX). Use this function when the positive boundary is required.

<a id="parse"></a>

## `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<i8, ParseError>
```

Reads the complete text as a signed decimal `i8`.

### Details

A failure contains `silk.format.NotANumber` for empty text, a leading `+`, a non-digit, or
trailing bytes. It contains `silk.format.OutOfRange` if the number is outside the `i8` range.
